intro_1: This is Forja, the programming environment of Dash for the Amiga.
intro_2: An editor, the compiler, the debugger, and editors for windows, sprites and maps, all on the Amiga itself.
intro_3: We will install it on CoffinOS and go through what it does, with an example of each thing.
instalar_1: Forja comes with Dash. This is the Dash 2.2 package, as it comes from its GitHub page.
instalar_2: It is unpacked with LhA, for example into RAM.
instalar_3: And its installer copies it wherever we say, and makes the dash command ready for any Shell.
instalar_4: Done. Forja is inside the Dash drawer.
editor_1: On the left, the files of the drawer. In the middle, the editor. Below, the output.
editor_2: We write a new program: a window with a greeting. The syntax colours help to read it.
editor_3: Amiga-E compiles it with Dash, right here on the Amiga, and runs it.
editor_4: There is the window. What the program prints comes out below, in the output.
errores_1: If something is wrong, the output says what it is and on which line.
errores_2: A click on the error takes the cursor to that line, to fix it.
depurar_1: To see what happens inside, the debugger. A click in the margin sets a breakpoint.
depurar_2: With F5, the program stops there. On the left, the stack and the variables with their values.
depurar_3: F10 steps one line. F5 goes on to the end.
ventanas_1: MUI windows are described in dashui files, and Forja opens them in its window editor.
ventanas_2: On the left, the tree of objects. On the right, their properties. We change the text of a button.
ventanas_3: Amiga-P shows the real window, with MUI, without compiling anything.
sprites_1: Amiga-B makes a hardware sprite or a BOB. We choose a BOB, the kind the blitter draws.
sprites_2: You draw with the pencil, the line, the box and the fill, with the colours of the palette.
sprites_3: We duplicate the frame and change it a little. The onion skin shows, with dots, what was in the previous one.
sprites_4: With space it plays animated. And the C key copies the Dash lines that load it.
mapas_1: For tile games there is the map editor. The tileset is a BOB from the sprite editor, with one frame for each tile.
mapas_2: You paint with the chosen tile. The fill does it in one go, and the box makes a block.
mapas_3: Layers go one on top of another. A collision layer marks what is ground, platform or ladder.
mapas_4: And objects say where the player and the enemies start. The game finds them by their kind.
juego_1: From Dash, tilemap_load loads the map and tilemap_draw draws it. This short program puts the little man where the player object is, and makes him walk on the collision layer.
juego_2: It is the same map we have just painted.
pantalla_1: In the preferences, Forja can open on a screen of its own, and the programs it runs come out there.
cierre_1: Forja and Dash are free. They are on GitHub, and at forja dot freemem dot space.
